description: CKAN (Comprehensive Kerbal Archive Network): mod manager for Kerbal Space Program. Finds, installs, updates and removes mods with their dependencies; GUI and command line. Self-contained .NET 10 build.
notes: Self-contained .NET 10 build (ckan-windows.exe, upstream's recommendation for Windows): no framework needed,
follows the Windows dark theme. gesu/CKAN-NetFx is the small .NET Framework build; only one of the two can be installed.
Update CKAN with 'scoop update CKAN': on the first start CKAN asks whether to check for its own updates
on launch; answer No. Its updater replaces the exe in the app folder behind Scoop's back.
CKAN keeps its settings, the list of game instances and the download cache (it can grow to gigabytes)
in %LOCALAPPDATA%\CKAN, and each game's list of installed mods in the CKAN folder inside the game folder.
'scoop uninstall -p' deletes neither. The cache folder and its size limit can be changed in CKAN's settings.
Mod changes fail while the game runs: Windows locks the mods' DLLs. Close KSP first.
CKAN refuses to start with administrator rights (an elevated shell, or any program when UAC is off).
The second shortcut, 'CKAN (--asroot)', starts it with --asroot, which skips that check. Files CKAN
then writes into the game folder belong to Administrators, so a non-elevated CKAN or KSP may not change them.
ckan:// links: on the first start CKAN offers to register them for all users, which needs admin rights (UAC).
'scoop uninstall CKAN' removes them if they point to this copy (from an elevated shell, if they were registered for all users).
pre_install: # Both packages add the command 'ckan': only one of them may be installed.

if ($cmd -eq 'install' -and (installed 'CKAN-NetFx')) { error "$app conflicts with CKAN-NetFx, which is installed. Run 'scoop uninstall CKAN-NetFx' first; CKAN's settings and caches in %LOCALAPPDATA%\CKAN stay. Scoop has already put ${app} into its app folder: run 'scoop uninstall $app' or simply install again, which cleans that up."; break }
# The DEV-tools bucket's ksp-ckan adds the same command 'ckan'.

if ($cmd -eq 'install' -and (installed 'ksp-ckan')) { error "$app conflicts with ksp-ckan (CKAN from another bucket), which is installed. Run 'scoop uninstall ksp-ckan' first; CKAN's settings and caches in %LOCALAPPDATA%\CKAN stay. Scoop has already put ${app} into its app folder: run 'scoop uninstall $app' or simply install again, which cleans that up."; break }

script: # CKAN registers ckan:// in HKCR, which lands in HKLM unless the key already exists for the current user.
# Remove it only if it points to this package's folder (trailing backslash: CKAN-NetFx's folder starts with the same name).
catch { warn "Could not remove the ckan:// link handler ($($key -replace ':', '')): run 'reg delete $($key -replace ':', '') /f' from an elevated shell." }
